newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends little changed after flurry on Brash.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends little changed after flurry on Brash.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed on Friday after opening lower on reported comments from Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6903/10 and 67.78 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.6907/14 and 67.91 at the opening.

The RBNZ stressed that Brash, speaking on Thursday in Sydney, had merely repeated his by now familiar theme that the Kiwi dollar was near the top of its cycle and the bank would prefer a mix of a lower currency and higher interest rates.
The Kiwi's falls were limited by U.S. dollar weakness and a steady Australian dollar, but dealers said the risk appeared on the downside for a possible test of 0.6850 next week.
One said Brash's view on the currency, despite his confessed inability to stipulate the monetary mix, were bound to have an effect over time.

Some offshore demand was emerging at lower levels and there was talk of possible samurai issues after euro activity earlier in the week, but Asian investors were not particularly keen buyers of New Zealand dollars on the day, he said.
The government's Budget Policy Statement on Tuesday, a set-piece outlining its fiscal intentions, is not expected to yield any great surprises or shake the financial markets.
